title: The per-channel area vector exists and removes the TFR aliasing, but every multi-area boundary is an assumed uniform split, not a measurement

goal.text: Every area-resolved LFP number in omission-a is computed from channels that belong to that area, and the manuscript states exactly how strongly that assignment is known.
goal.falsifier: Closed when either (a) the channel-to-area boundaries are replaced by an anatomically or physiologically estimated boundary with a receipt, or (b) the manuscript states in Methods that the boundaries are an equal-share assumption and no claim in the paper rests on a channel's area assignment near a segment boundary.

notes: STEP 3a of the four-step plan. Script: scripts/build_channel_area_vector.py. Outputs: outputs/channel_area_vector/channel_area_vector.csv, partition_audit.csv, receipt.json.

ALIASING FIX CONFIRMED. scripts/archive_oneoff/precompute_tfr_arrays.py writes, for a probe spanning k areas, k files that are the SAME full 128-channel array under k different area tokens (its own comment: 'Build full-probe TFR once per condition, then save per area label (same array; naming uses each area token)'). Selecting only the channels the area vector assigns to a file's area token removes the overlap: every channel now contributes to exactly one area.

COVERAGE: 6,528 channels across 51 probes in all 17 TFR-corpus sessions. 0 unresolved area tokens -- every (session, probe, area) filename token in D:/workspace/data/tfr_arrays resolves to at least one channel. 12 areas: FEF, FST, MST, MT, PFC, TEO, V1, V2, V3, V3a, V3d, V4.

CROSS-CHECK PASSED: all 6,528 per-channel area labels in D:/workspace/data/metadata/<session>/electrodes.csv agree with the channel_slices partition in probe_areas.json. Zero disagreements. The two sidecars are consistent -- which means they share an origin, not that either is independently correct.

THE FINDING. 27 of 51 probes span more than one area. In 26 of those 27, the boundary sits at channel 64 of 128 -- exactly half. The 27th is the only three-area probe (sub-C31o_ses-230823 probe C, 'V1, V2, V3') and its boundaries are 42 and 85 -- exactly thirds. Every multi-area partition in the corpus is an exact uniform division of the channel axis in area listing order. No boundary is anatomically or physiologically estimated.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT BUY. It buys disjointness: area labels no longer alias the same data, so between-area contrasts are no longer partly a probe against itself. It does not buy anatomy: it does not establish that a given channel sits in the area its label names. A channel near a segment boundary is assigned by an assumption of equal share, and the true boundary is unknown.

MANUSCRIPT CONSEQUENCE. The Methods sentence adopted from context/04_draft_biorxiv_markdown.md -- 'its ordered channel axis was partitioned into contiguous segments corresponding to those listed areas' -- is accurate but incomplete as written. It describes the operation without disclosing that the segment widths are equal by assumption. Left as-is it reads as though a boundary was estimated. It must say the partition is an equal-share assignment in probe listing order.

A HARDER CONSEQUENCE FOR THE V3 CLAIM. V3d and V3a are the two halves of one probe, split at channel 64 by assumption. Any statement contrasting V3d with V3a is a statement about the upper versus lower half of a single shank, not about two areas. The two labels should be pooled to V3a/d for inference, or the contrast dropped.
issues: Segment widths are uniform by construction in 27/27 multi-area probes; no boundary in the corpus is measured.
V3d vs V3a is an intra-probe half-split contrast and cannot support a between-area claim.
electrodes.csv agreeing with probe_areas.json is not independent corroboration -- the per-channel labels are materialized from the same slices.

scripts/archive_oneoff/build_channel_layer_mapping.py had a stale REPO_ROOT (parents[1], correct only while the file sat directly in scripts/) and crashed at import with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'codes'. Fixed to parents[2]. The vFLIP layer products were therefore never regenerated after the refactor that moved the script -- only one session's *_channel_layers.csv existed on disk, from before the move.
plan: Pool V3d and V3a into a single V3a/d level for any inferential model; keep them separate only in descriptive per-channel displays.
Amend the Methods partition sentence in context/omission-a-draft-v1.md to state the equal-share assumption explicitly.

If a measured boundary is wanted later, the vFLIP2 per-segment crossover and the pairwise LFP correlation block structure already computed in build_channel_layer_mapping.py are the natural estimators -- but that is a new analysis, not a correction.

verification.receipt: scripts/build_channel_area_vector.py run 2026-07-28: 6,528 channels, 17/17 sessions, 51 probes, 0 unresolved area tokens, 0 electrodes.csv disagreements. partition_audit.csv segment_widths value counts: [64, 64] x 26, [42, 43, 43] x 1; contiguous_and_complete true for all 51 probes. The uniform-split test compares each probe's segment widths against numpy.array_split of its channel axis.

links.reasoning: Channel selection by the area vector makes area labels disjoint, which is the specific defect that node recorded.
v1's Methods records the contiguous-segment partition as though the boundaries were determined; they are assumed equal. The sentence needs amending before v2.
Same class of defect from the opposite direction: there a number was asserted without a computation, here a computation is real but its input assignment is an undisclosed assumption.
